metaDescription: Six dusk to dawn LED bulbs compared on lumens, color temperature, photocell behavior, bug-light amber, vintage style, pack size and fixture limits.
expertTake: The Feit Electric A21 is our top pick because its listing states 1500 lumens, 90 plus CRI and a five-color-temperature choice in a dusk-to-dawn bulb, which is rare. The TORCHSTAR 4-pack is the value pick for a sensor bulb at a stated 800 lumens and 9 W. Skip the category if you want a light you can switch on at will, because a photocell bulb turns on by itself at dusk and will not stay off in the dark.
introParagraphs: A dusk-to-dawn bulb has a light sensor in the base that turns the bulb on when it gets dark and off in daylight, so a porch, a garage door or a path light comes on without a timer. It is a simple security and convenience bulb, and it suits fixtures where nobody wants to flip a switch. The catches are that the sensor must see daylight, the bulb cannot be turned off on demand and many models cannot be dimmed.

We evaluated each bulb from its published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, not from installing it. Listings differ in whether they state lumens, color temperature and rating, and we say so where a figure is missing. The lineup spans standard household bulbs, a high-output bulb, an amber bug light and a vintage Edison style so you can match the bulb to the fixture.

products.name: Feit Electric A21 LED Dusk-to-Dawn Bulb, 100W Eq, 5CCT, 1500 Lumens, 90+ CRI
products.description:
The Feit Electric A21 is a dusk-to-dawn LED bulb of 100W equivalent, with 1500 lumens at 16.5 W, a five-color-temperature selection, a CRI above 90 and an E26 base. The listing says the built-in sensor detects ambient light and switches the bulb automatically. It is the brightest bulb in the lineup and the only one that lets you choose the white.

The tradeoff is size and fixture fit. An A21 bulb is longer and wider than an A19, so it may not fit a small fixture or an enclosed globe, and 16.5 W of heat in an enclosed fixture can shorten the bulb's life. A color selector is a switch you set once. Compared with the TORCHSTAR, it is much brighter and has better color.

Check the fixture's maximum wattage and clearance before buying. It suits a large porch, a garage or a yard fixture where bright, high-quality, selectable light is wanted.
products.bestFor: Large porches and garages that want a bright, color-accurate sensor bulb with selectable white.
pros: Stated 1500 lumens is the brightest output in the lineup
Five selectable color temperatures let you match the fixture
CRI above 90 shows colors more accurately than basic bulbs
Built-in sensor needs no app or hub
cons: A21 shape may not fit small fixtures or enclosed globes
16.5 W of heat in an enclosed fixture can shorten bulb life

products.name: TORCHSTAR 4-Pack Dusk to Dawn LED Bulb, A19, 9 W, 800 Lumens, 5000K, Photocell
products.description:
The TORCHSTAR is a four-pack of A19 dusk-to-dawn LED bulbs at 9 W and 800 lumens in 5000K daylight, with a photocell sensor that the listing says works in fixtures or near other lights, and UL, FCC and DOE listings. The listing says the bulbs turn on at night and off in the daytime. It is the best-priced multi-pack in the lineup.

The tradeoff is color and sensor. A 5000K daylight white looks cold and blue next to a warm porch light, and a photocell can misread if another light shines near the bulb, though the listing says it handles that. An 800 lumen bulb is a standard 60W equivalent. Compared with the GE, it comes in a four-pack and is cooler in tone.

Use it in fixtures that see daylight and avoid putting the sensor under a deep hood. It suits several porch or garage fixtures where daylight white and a low pack cost matter.
products.bestFor: Several fixtures that need a daylight-white sensor bulb at a low pack cost.
pros: Four bulbs in a pack suit several fixtures at once
Stated 800 lumens at 9 W is a standard 60W equivalent
Photocell sensor is described as working near other fixtures
UL, FCC and DOE listings are stated on the product
cons: 5000K daylight white looks cool and bluish next to warm fixtures
Sensor can still misread if another light shines close to the bulb

products.name: GE LED+ A19 Dusk to Dawn LED Bulbs, Soft White, 2 Pack, Automatic On/Off Security

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Built-in sensor, no app, hub or switch

products.description:
The GE LED+ is a two-pack of A19 dusk-to-dawn bulbs in soft white with a standard E26 base and a built-in sensor that the listing says needs no app, hub or switch. The listing describes the bulb as an outdoor security light that gives the impression someone is home. It is the warmest standard white in the lineup.

The tradeoff is detail. The text we reviewed gives no lumen or wattage figure, so brightness has to be checked on the page, and soft white is warmer but less crisp than daylight. A two-pack is enough for a front and back door. Compared with the TORCHSTAR, it is warmer and states less.

Screw it into a fixture that sees daylight and check the lumen figure on the listing page. It suits a front porch where a warm, simple security bulb is wanted.

products.name: DAYBETTER 4 Pack A19 Dusk to Dawn Bulbs, 9 W, 800 Lumens, 5000K, 60W Equivalent
products.description:
The DAYBETTER is a four-pack of A19 dusk-to-dawn bulbs with a photocell sensor, 800 lumens at 9 W as a 60W equivalent and a steady 5000K daylight white. The listing says the bulbs turn on and off automatically for a porch and for security. It is almost identical in specification to the TORCHSTAR.

The tradeoff is sameness. At 5000K it is a cool white, and it states no CRI or rating. A four-pack is a lot of bulbs if you need only one. Compared with the TORCHSTAR, it is similar in output and states less on listings and approvals.

Check the lumen figure and the fixture size before buying. It suits a house with several outdoor fixtures where a four-pack of daylight white bulbs is wanted.

products.name: Qualilux Dusk to Dawn A19 LED Bug Light Bulbs, 1900K Amber, 600 Lumens, 9.5 W, 2 Pack

specList.label: Sensor
specList.value: Photocell, no app or manual setting

products.description:
The Qualilux is a two-pack of dusk-to-dawn A19 bug light bulbs in 1900K amber yellow at 600 lumens and 9.5 W, with a photocell sensor that needs no app or manual setting and a smart driver chip to cut energy waste. The listing says the amber glow is cozy. It is the warmest bulb in the lineup.

The tradeoff is brightness and coverage. An amber 1900K bulb is dim for security and shows little color, and bug lights reduce the attraction of insects rather than eliminate it. At 600 lumens, it is below the 800 of a standard bulb. Compared with the GE, it is warmer and dimmer.

Use it on a porch where insects gather and the mood matters more than reading light. It suits a porch, a patio or a deck where a warm, low-attraction glow is wanted.

products.name: Qualilux Dusk to Dawn ST19 Edison LED Bulbs, Amber Glass, 2300K, 6.5 W, Non-Dimmable
products.description:
The Qualilux Edison is a pack of dusk-to-dawn ST19 vintage LED bulbs in dark amber brown glass with filaments, 2300K amber warm light, 6.5 W as a 60W equivalent and a photocell sensor with no app or manual setting. The listing says the bulbs are non-dimmable. It is the most decorative bulb in the lineup.

The tradeoff is style over output. Amber glass cuts brightness and the listing gives no lumen figure in the text we reviewed, so it is a mood bulb for an exposed fixture and not a security light. Non-dimmable means it will flicker on a dimmer. Compared with the amber bug light, it has a vintage shape and a slightly cooler color.

Use it in an open fixture where the filament shape shows. It suits an exposed-bulb porch light, a gazebo or a pergola where a vintage look is the point.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A photocell reads ambient light and switches the bulb. It must see daylight, so a deep hood, a dark soffit or a nearby light can confuse it. The TORCHSTAR says its sensor works near other fixtures. Put the bulb where it sees the sky and check it after a week. A bulb under a deep eave may stay on all day, and one beside a bright window may never come on, so the position matters more than the brand.

The Feit lists 1500 lumens, the TORCHSTAR and DAYBETTER 800, the Qualilux bug light 600, and the GE gives none. A porch needs roughly 400 to 800 lumens, and a large yard more. Watts tell you the draw, not the light. A path needs far less than a driveway, and over-bright porch bulbs annoy neighbors and wash out the view of the garden at night.

5000K, as on the TORCHSTAR and DAYBETTER, is cool daylight white, soft white is warmer, and amber at 1900K to 2300K is the warmest. Cool white looks more like security light, warm light is more welcoming. Pick one color for fixtures that are in view together. A porch with one cool bulb and one warm bulb looks accidental, and mixed temperatures are easy to avoid by buying a multi-pack.

A21 and ST19 bulbs are bigger than A19. Enclosed fixtures trap heat and shorten LED life, and bulbs must be rated for them. Check the maximum wattage and the clearance. Do not use a bulb in a fixture it does not fit. Check the fixture's label for its maximum wattage and whether it is rated for enclosed or damp use, and replace any cracked sockets before installing a new bulb.

Dusk-to-dawn bulbs are on whenever it is dark, so a switch cannot keep them off, and most are not dimmable. The Qualilux Edison is stated non-dimmable. Put the fixture on a switch if you want to turn the light off at will, and remember that a switch that is off also keeps the sensor from working, so leave it on for the automatic function.

A four-pack, like the TORCHSTAR and DAYBETTER, suits a house with many fixtures, while a two-pack suits a front and back door. Sensors can fail before the LED. Keep a spare and note the purchase date. A bulb that fails within the first months is easier to return when you have the date, and a spare bulb saves a dark porch for a week.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each bulb from the lumens, color temperature, size and sensor stated on its Amazon listing. We did not install any of them. The Feit's 1500 lumens and the TORCHSTAR's 800 lumens are numbers we compare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Numbers over claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked bulbs that state lumens and color above those that do not. Where a listing gave neither, we say so. That is why the Feit ranks first.

howWeEvaluated.title: On-topic filtering
howWeEvaluated.description: The topic search returned candelabra and other shapes from the same makers. We kept the A19, A21 and vintage shapes that suit common fixtures. That left a lineup of six.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered recurring themes such as sensors misreading near other lights, short life in enclosed fixtures and cool light looking harsh. We do not repeat ratings or counts. A pattern counted only when it matched the described design.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: No listing here states a measured sensor lux threshold. We say so plainly. Sensor behavior depends on the fixture and its surroundings.

cards.label: Cool white
cards.text: The TORCHSTAR, DAYBETTER and Feit set to 5000K look like security lights. They attract insects and look stark.

cards.label: Warm amber
cards.text: The Qualilux bug and Edison bulbs glow cozy and draw fewer insects. They are dimmer.

howToChoose.note: Choose cool white for security and warm amber for porches where mood matters.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A bulb that fits the fixture, a warm color for welcome and a sensor that sees daylight. Check the wet or damp rating of the fixture.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GE LED+ and Qualilux bug light both suit porches, with the GE brighter and the Qualilux warmer.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a smart bulb with an app, a timer you can set or a dimmable sensor bulb. Those sit above these simple sensor bulbs.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a bulb that comes on at night. A basic pack like the TORCHSTAR covers that.

maintenance.interval: After one week, then every 3 months
maintenance.why: Dirt or a nearby light can confuse it. Wipe the sensor and check the on and off times.
Dust and cobwebs dim output. Wipe the glass when it is cool.
Sensors can fail before the LED. Keep a spare from the same pack.
Water in a fixture shortens bulb life. Seal the fixture and dry it.
Confirm the bulb comes on at dusk and goes off at dawn. Adjust placement if it cycles.

faq.q: Can I turn a dusk-to-dawn bulb off?
faq.a: Only by cutting power at the switch. The bulb comes on whenever it is dark.

faq.q: Do these bulbs work with a dimmer?
faq.a: Usually not. The Qualilux Edison states non-dimmable, and most others are not designed for dimmers.

faq.q: Why does my bulb flicker on and off?
faq.a: The sensor can see its own light or a nearby light. Move it or shield the sensor.
They attract fewer insects but do not eliminate them. Amber light is less attractive than white.

faq.q: Can I use them in an enclosed fixture?
faq.a: Only if the bulb is rated for it. Heat shortens LED life.

faq.q: What color is best for a porch?
faq.a: Soft white or amber is welcoming, and 5000K is a security look.
